newsitem.title: USA: Dow snaps losing streak, aided by solid 3M results.
newsitem.headline: Dow snaps losing streak, aided by solid 3M results.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks snapped a four-session losing streak Friday and climbed back above 6,000, bolstered by an unexpectedly strong earnings report from Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co., one of the stocks in the Dow Jones industrial average.
The Dow industrials rose 14.54 to 6,007.02 after falling 44 points on Thursday and ending below 6,000 for the first time in two weeks. For the week, the index lost 87.21 points.

"Investors are taking a stand at the 6,000 mark and there's a normal adjustment to the sell-off of recent sessions," said Jim Solloway, director of research at Argus Research. He noted the market got a lift from 3M, whose gains accounted for about nine points of the Dow's rise.
In the broader market, losers led gainers, 1,247 to 1,076, on moderate volume of about 365 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange, off from 415 million on Thursday.
The Nasdaq composite index fell 4.40 points to close at 1,222.60.

Stocks were pressured from the start after bond prices fell on news that orders for expensive manufactured goods rose a surprisingly strong 4.6 percent last month, the biggest jump since December 1992.
But bonds later rebounded after investors saw that most of the jump came from a big rise in aircraft orders, which fluctuate widely from month to month.

The rally in the bond market lent support to stocks as long-term interest rates fell. The 30-year Treasury bond added 14/32, or $4.375 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, to 6.82 percent from 6.85 percent on Thursday.

3M surged 3-1/8 to 74-3/8, and touched a 52-week high of 74-1/2, after the company said earnings rose 16 percent in the third quarter, its first quarter since spinning off the data storage and imaging businesses that had restrained 3M's results.

Trading slowed in the afternoon as Wall Street braced for next week's reports on labour costs in the third quarter and October consumer confidence, both due on Tuesday, the first look at third quarter gross domestic product, due on Wednesday, and Friday's key October jobs report.
Analysts said the market was likely to remain under pressure unless there is surprisingly good news.

"The market is still in a short-term corrective cycle. There's limited upside surprise potential and more likely vulnerability unless we have new evidence that inflation is under control," said Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst with Janney, Montgomery Scott.
Peggy Farley, chief executive of Amas Securities, said the market was in a holding pattern ahead of next week's reports.
Among individual shares, Chubb climbed 5-1/2 to 51 after telling analysts in a conference call it was mulling the possible sale of its life and real estate businesses.

Some drug stocks were weaker after recent strength. Bristol Myers lost 2-3/4 to 105-3/4, Schering-Plough was off 2-1/4 to 64-1/4, Eli Lilly fell 2 to 69-3/4 and Dow component Merck shed 1-3/4 to 73-3/8.

Aetna rose 3 to 63-1/8 after defying uncertainty elsewhere in the health care insurance industry by meeting analysts' expectations for third-quarter earnings. Its results included the newly acquired U.S. Healthcare.
Among new issues, Triumph Group, an aircraft component maker, rose 2-3/4 to 21-3/4, and Metris Cos., a direct marketer of consumer products, surged 4-3/8 to 20-3/8.
P.J. America, with 42 Papa John's pizza stores, jumped 3-7/8 to 16-3/8 in its first day of trading. Stage Stores, which operates clothing stores, rallied 2-3/4 to 19-1/4.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 1.37 points to 700.92. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.01 to 569.79.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.52 to 373.26. The average share lost 5 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,834.311, down 9.723 or 0.14 percent.
